profiles.name: Katie Lee
profiles.excerpt: Katie Lee moved from Hollywood radio acting into a celebrated career as a folk singer, writer and outspoken defender of Glen Canyon.
profiles.bio_html:
Katie Lee was born in Tucson in 1919 and studied drama at the University of Arizona before moving to Hollywood. She worked as an actress in film, television and radio, including recurring appearances on The Great Gildersleeve, The Railroad Hour and The Halls of Ivy.

By the mid-1950s Lee had shifted the center of her career to folk music, performing in major clubs, recording albums and becoming especially identified with songs of the American West and Colorado River country. Her singing career ultimately became more important to her public identity than acting.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight The Railroad Hour broadcasts featuring Lee, two Roy Rogers appearances and one The Great Gildersleeve performance. Those credits remain linked to her acting history while her primary category reflects the folk-singing career for which she became best known.
